classification.difficultyReason: Use positivity of the exponential to analyse derivative signs, assemble the scaffolded sketch and range, then recognise the reflected function as f(-x).

children.label: a
children.prompt: Where is the function zero, positive and negative? Is it even, odd or neither?

answer.short: Zero at $x=0$, positive for $x>0$, negative for $x<0$; neither even nor odd.
answer.worked: Since $e^x>0$, $xe^x$ has the same sign as $x$. Also $f(-x)=-xe^{-x}$, which is neither $f(x)$ nor $-f(x)$ as an identity. Hence the function is neither even nor odd.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Show that there is one stationary point, and determine its nature.

answer.short: One stationary point: a minimum at $(-1,-e^{-1})$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}(1+x)e^x&=0\\x&=-1,\\y(-1)&=-e^{-1}.\end{aligned}$$
Since $e^x>0$, the sign of $y'$ is the sign of $1+x$.
$$\begin{array}{c|ccc}x&x<-1&-1&x>-1\\\hline y'&-&0&+\\\text{slope}&\text{decreasing}&\text{stationary}&\text{increasing}\end{array}$$
Thus the unique stationary point is a minimum.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Find the coordinates of the lone point of inflection.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}(2+x)e^x&=0\\x&=-2,\\y(-2)&=-2e^{-2}.\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{array}{c|ccc}x&x<-2&-2&x>-2\\\hline y''&-&0&+\\\text{concavity}&\text{down}&&\text{up}\end{array}$$
The concavity changes at $x=-2$, so the lone point of inflection is $(-2,-2e^{-2})$.
As $x\to\infty$, each of $xe^x$, $(1+x)e^x$ and $(2+x)e^x$ tends to $\infty$. The curve is eventually above the $x$-axis and increasing at an increasing rate.

children.label: f
children.prompt: Given that $y\to0$ as $x\to-\infty$, sketch the curve, then write down its range.

answer.short: Range: $y\ge-\frac{1}{e}$. The graph has minimum $(-1,-e^{-1})$ and inflection point $(-2,-2e^{-2})$, and passes through the origin.
answer.worked:
The curve approaches $y=0$ from below as $x\to-\infty$. It decreases to $(-1,-e^{-1})$, then increases through $(0,0)$ without bound. It is concave down for $x<-2$ and concave up for $x>-2$, with inflection point $(-2,-2e^{-2})$. It also passes through $(1,e)$.

The minimum value is $-\frac{1}{e}$, so the range is $[-\frac{1}{e},\infty)$.

spec.description: Left member of the reflection pair, including labelled minimum and inflection point with curved leaders and dashed guides to (1,e).

children.label: g
children.prompt: Hence also sketch $y=-xe^{-x}$ by recognising the simple transformation.

answer.short: Reflect $y=xe^x$ in the $y$-axis. Minimum $(1,-e^{-1})$; inflection point $(2,-2e^{-2})$.
answer.worked:
For $f(x)=xe^x$,
$$f(-x)=(-x)e^{-x}=-xe^{-x}.$$
Reflect the graph in the $y$-axis: $(x,y)$ maps to $(-x,y)$. The minimum becomes $(1,-e^{-1})$, the inflection point becomes $(2,-2e^{-2})$, and $(1,e)$ becomes $(-1,e)$. The origin stays fixed. The graph rises without bound to the left and approaches $y=0$ from below to the right.

spec.description: Right member of the reflection pair, with the same coordinate units and vertical scale as the left graph; curved leaders identify the minimum and inflection point, and dashed guides mark (-1,e).
spec.mathematics: y=-xe^{-x}=f(-x), reflection of y=xe^x in the y-axis.
